name: Light Cendre Green
lede: Light Cendre Green is a pale yellowish green from Ridgway's 1912 atlas, filed again by name in the 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary, and one of the rarest named colors in our painting archive.

sections.title: A Ridgway tone, scarce in paint
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Color Nomenclature* carries this swatch on plate VI, hue 35, tone d [1]. The 1955 ISCC-NBS dictionary files the exact name "Light Cendre Green" under block 130, "brilliant yellowish green" [2]. The name builds the modifier "light" onto [[cendre-green]], "cendre" being the French word for ash, describing the family's greyed quality rather than this specific tint's own story [1].

In our color library its closest neighbor is [[granny-smith-apple]], about 3.0 units away and more vivid, followed by [[light-grey-green]] at 3.1 units, close enough to pass for the same color [3]. [[hospital-green]] sits 4.6 units off and greener [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings matches this tone in only 4 of them, about 0.02 percent, as photographed, rarer than 86 percent of the named colors we track [4]. The sample is too small here to support a century, painter or country reading, so we report only presence and rank. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, and the match is a computed color reading, not a pigment identification [4].
